interpretation: The 3, 2.5 and 2 mm PaStiX/native-default study and the separate 2/1.5 mm SPOOLES1 study keep reconstructed CAD, material, physical load/fixture boxes and 37 g battery COM/rigid patch fixed.
Equal per-node force distribution and discrete patch membership vary with the mesh.
The two 2 mm backend anchors have exactly equal principal metrics, six eigenfrequencies and mesh metadata; the only baseline vector component difference is about 1.26e-12 mm.
The historical free candidate passes the final 2 to 1.5 mm sensitivity screen with SPOOLES1: stiffness 0.0013%, displacement 0.8755%, first frequency 0.4669%, stress 0.5934%.
The baseline stress peak increases 22.0235% in that interval, above the unchanged 5% criterion. General mesh convergence and a converged stress-based candidate/v0 ratio are not established.
All five historical candidate/v0 acceptance comparisons pass at every complete mesh/backend level. A passed final interval for one geometry is not an asymptotic convergence proof.
The original native-default/two-thread 1.5 mm baseline modal crash remains a failed record. A separated, explicit SPOOLES1 study supplies new complete results without replacing it.

Source changes for explicit backend choice and subsequent invalid-input metadata validation intentionally invalidate exact resume against earlier source identities; every run has its complete source-byte archive.
